CRIMINAL
APPEAL NO.532 OF 2023

 RAVINDRA @ ROBIN & ORS. ... APPE

VS.
 STATE OF UTTARAKHAND & ANR. ...
RESP  O R D E R Leave granted.
Heard the learned senior counsel appearing for the appellants and the learned counsel appearing for the first respondent.
Office report records that respondent No.2 has been duly served.
We have perused the complaint filed by respondent No.2.
Going by the averments made in the complaint, the appellant No.1 and respondent No.2 were in relationship right from the year 2016 till May, 2020.
The allegation is that on 3rd May, 2020, the appellant No.1 telephonically refused to marry respondent No.2.
Following are relevant and important factual aspects to be noted:

(i) Before the second respondent lodged the complaint alleging commission of offences under Section 376 (2)(n), 323 and 504 IPC, the appellant No.1 had lodged a complaint against respondent No.2 which is placed on record on 12th November,
2020 and (ii) Even respondent No.2 has accepted that she was a married woman.
She claimed that her marriage was not in subsistence as her husband had married to a muslim girl.

However, it is not the case of respondent No.2 that the marriage was dissolved by order of Ravindra @ Robin vs The State Of Uttarakhand on 20 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/8677743/
1 competent court.

sentences.text: Reliance is placed by the appellants on order dated 27th July, 2022 in Criminal Appeal No.422 of 2022 in the case of Mandar Deepak Pawar v. The State of Maharashtra & Anr.

entities.text: Mandar Deepak Pawar v. The State of Maharashtra & Anr
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
In the present case,
even respondent No.2 was aware of the obstacles in getting married with appellant No.1.
Notwithstanding the said knowledge, she continued to be in relationship for a long period of four years with appellant No.1.
Hence, we are of the view that on a plain reading of the assertions made by respondent No.2 in the complaint, no offence was made out against the appellants.
Accordingly, the impugned order is set aside.
Further proceedings on the basis of the FIR No.642/2020 dated 27th November, 2020 registered at Police Station Kotwali Roorkee, District Haridwar are hereby quashed.
The appeal is accordingly allowed.
